questions.question: What shape are hazardous material warning signs?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: When you approach your vehicle, you should check for:

options.text: Whether the vehicle is parked far from others.
Puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: Puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle for damage or leaning. Look under it for fresh leaks. Check around it for hazards like other vehicles, people, or low wires.

questions.question: You are driving slowly in a construction zone and see a worker near the road. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Always drive slowly through construction areas. Drive even slower when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the drinks were consumed

questions.explanation: A person's BAC depends on three things: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it is consumed, and the person's weight. The temperature of the drinks does not matter.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving, shipping papers should be:
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in another place the driver can easily reach while wearing a seat belt. The papers must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Frequent blinking is a sign of fatigue.
questions.explanation: Frequent blinking, trouble focusing, and heavy eyelids are warning signs of fatigue. If you are tired, stop driving and leave the road.

questions.question: When driving a new vehicle, you should learn the controls:

options.text: Only if you feel you need to.

questions.explanation: Learn how to use all the controls and features of a new vehicle before you start driving.

questions.question: When driving a combination vehicle, you should make:
questions.explanation: Brake early and look far ahead when driving a combination vehicle. This helps prevent your trailer from jackknifing.

questions.question: Passive railroad crossings:

options.text: Have gates that lower when trains approach.
Should never be crossed by a CMV.

questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: What is a trolley valve used for?
questions.explanation: The trolley valve controls trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause skids. Never use it while parking because it may release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.
Do not use a turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: When passing a pedestrian or another vehicle, assume they do not see you.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid being blinded by headlights at night?

options.text: Close your eyes as vehicles approach.
Look to the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights, glance to the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: Is rough acceleration good or bad?

options.text: It is fine at slow speeds.
It is fine at all speeds.
It is bad because it can damage the vehicle.
It is bad because it confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is bad because it can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and parts.

questions.question: If there is a truck fire, what should you do before opening trailer doors?

options.text: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Before opening trailer doors during a fire, touch them to check if they are hot. If they are hot, there may be a cargo fire inside. Keep the doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.explanation: If another driver is aggressive, move out of their way. Do not provoke them by making eye contact, racing, or refusing to move. Ignore any rude gestures.

questions.question: When backing up, is using a helper a good idea?

options.text: No, it is illegal in most states.

questions.explanation: Use a helper when backing up. The helper should watch the vehicle's blind spots and stand in a place where the driver can see them.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Read the manual first. Then take hazardous materials training courses and learn the federal and state rules for transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does that affect your braking distance?
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, your braking distance becomes four times longer. Higher speeds mean more power and longer stopping distances.

questions.question: In bad weather, what do many car drivers do around trucks?

options.text: Drive to the sides of trucks.

questions.explanation: In bad weather with poor visibility, many car drivers follow trucks too closely.
